task_spec: Generalize traktor_nml_tool.py's stale-path reconnection to work against an arbitrary set of scanned filesystem locations (not just a second NML file), and add splice/split commands to merge or partition NML collection files while keeping playlists valid

scope: local NML fixture corpus at C:\codex\general_tasks\collection_textual_patch_test.nml and C:\codex\general_tasks\tmp_traktor_lxml\*.nml, C:\codex\general_tasks\tmp_traktor_test\*.nml (used for schema verification and test fixtures)
out-of-scope: acoustic-fingerprinting online lookup (AcoustID/MusicBrainz network queries) - fingerprinting is local-only comparison between two computed fingerprints
out-of-scope: full playlist-tree-preserving splice/split (nested folder structure, smartlist criteria) - v1 is a flat playlist-entry merge/subset tool

out-of-scope: Traktor session-history support - confirmed absent from this NML schema version (VERSION=20, Traktor Pro 4); SETS/SET (Remix Sets) is a distinct unrelated feature, passed through untouched
constraints: MUST: preserve the existing byte-preserving lxml text-patch write invariant - reconnection writes only ever change intended LOCATION/PRIMARYKEY attribute values, nothing else in the file changes
MUST: never silently guess on ambiguity - ambiguous/unmatched/conflicting cases must always be reported (stats + CSV export), never silently resolved
MUST: one-to-one assignment invariant for disk reconnection - no disk candidate may be assigned to more than one old track; destination collisions are excluded from rewrite and reported as ambiguous

MUST: explicit VOLUME/VOLUMEID identity on every rewritten LOCATION - inference from existing collection paths allowed only when unambiguous, otherwise --volume-map is required, never silently guessed

MUST: splice defaults to fail-on-conflict, not silently keep-first; a persistent conflict report is always written even when --on-conflict overrides the default, so cues/grids/ratings/other track state is never silently discarded
MUST: dry-run before write; refuse to write when output path equals input path (existing tool convention)
MUST: zero-write-on-ambiguity/error - any unresolved ambiguity, destination collision, or mid-run error aborts the entire write for that output file, no partial writes
SHOULD: reuse existing abstractions (record_keys/match_records cascade, ElemPatch/apply_text_patches, _process_non_collection_*_entries cascade) rather than duplicating matching/write logic

SHOULD: follow existing CLI conventions - dry-run flags, key=value stats output, CSV export via location_rows/csv.DictWriter pattern, subcommand naming matching existing verb/verb-noun/verb-from-noun patterns

rejected_alternatives: Building a separate/parallel matching cascade for disk-scan candidates - rejected because record_keys/match_records already generalize cleanly if disk files are wrapped as EntryRecord with entry=None; duplicating would create a second cascade to keep in sync

Generalizing apply_text_patches/ElemPatch to handle whole-node insert/remove for splice/split - rejected because it is attribute-substitution only by design; forcing structural edits through it would be a hack or silently fall back to the non-byte-preserving stdlib serialization path. A new, separate span-transplantation primitive is used instead

Defaulting splice's conflict policy to keep-first - rejected as the initial default because it can silently discard divergent metadata (cues/grids/ratings) between two sources' copies of 'the same' track; fail-by-default was chosen instead with keep-first/keep-last as explicit opt-in via --on-conflict, always paired with a persistent conflict report

Inferring VOLUME/VOLUMEID from old collection paths as a fallback of last resort after a full drive/mount change - rejected because post-move, old paths are exactly the unreliable signal; inference is only used when unambiguous, otherwise an explicit --volume-map flag is required
General arbitrary filter/selector language for split (folder/artist/date-range/entry-list clauses) - rejected by explicit user decision in favor of a simpler named-playlist-only filter scope for v1

Including Traktor session-history support in splice/split v1 - rejected/moot once schema verification showed no HISTORY container exists in this NML version; SETS/SET is an unrelated feature (Remix Sets) and is passed through untouched

Serializing every non-base fragment via ET.tostring() in splice - rejected in favor of span-transplantation-by-default (byte-exact copy of source spans) for fidelity; ET.tostring() retained only as an explicit fallback for fragments that are actually modified (renames, PRIMARYKEY redirects)
current_understanding: traktor_nml_tool.py is a single-file Python CLI (optional lxml, stdlib ET fallback) with 7 existing subcommands: inspect, encode-dir, preview-diff, preview-compare, scan-compare-candidates, rewrite, rewrite-from-collection-compare

The tool's core domain model: LOCATION elements (VOLUME/VOLUMEID/DIR/FILE) on COLLECTION entries; PRIMARYKEY (VOLUME+DIR+FILE concatenation) on PLAYLIST/history entries as a flattened reference back to a collection entry

Two existing rewrite strategies: rule-based (explicit old->new volume/dir prefix rules) and compare-based (match old collection against a newer collection file via the record_keys/match_records tiered cascade), both converging on the same ElemPatch/apply_text_patches byte-preserving write path

Confirmed NML schema (via direct inspection of the real 6412-entry fixture): COLLECTION ENTRIES=N; PLAYLISTS contains nested NODE TYPE=FOLDER (wrapping SUBNODES COUNT=N) and NODE TYPE=PLAYLIST (wrapping one PLAYLIST ENTRIES=N TYPE=LIST UUID=... containing ENTRY/PRIMARYKEY TYPE=TRACK|STEM KEY=... children, or self-closed when empty); a top-level INDEXING/SORTING_INFO section (keyed by backslash-separated playlist path) lists per-playlist sort criteria, separate from the PLAYLISTS tree; SETS/SET is Remix Sets, unrelated to history; no HISTORY container exists in this schema version

Full design plan already exists and was iteratively reviewed at C:\ClaudeProjects\claude_design_PCFS\claude-config\traktor_nml_tool_plan.md - Phase 0 (shared refactors), Phase 1 (disk-scan reconnection), Phase 2 (splice/split) are all fully specified including acceptance criteria, testing/rollout plan, and a status section confirming both phases are ready to implement
assumptions: Schema verified against VERSION=20 / Traktor Pro 4 only (H confidence for this version; other Traktor versions not spot-checked, noted as a residual open item in the plan)

mutagen and pyacoustid/fpcalc (chromaprint) are acceptable new dependencies for tag reading and acoustic fingerprinting respectively, gated behind HAS_LXML-style import guards (H confidence, consistent with existing optional-dependency pattern in the tool)

Traktor will tolerate a fresh UUID on a renamed/collided imported playlist rather than requiring UUID continuity (M confidence - not verified against actual Traktor import behavior, flagged in the plan's Testing & Rollout section as requiring manual Traktor import/open validation)
invisible_knowledge: Hard invariant: reconnection writes (Phase 1) only ever change LOCATION and PRIMARYKEY attribute values via the existing apply_text_patches mechanism - every other byte of the source file is preserved exactly, and nothing in Phase 1 introduces a second write path

One-to-one assignment invariant (Phase 1): match_records' existing ambiguity detection only catches source-side ambiguity (multiple candidates for one old track); it does NOT catch destination-side collisions (multiple old tracks converging on one new candidate) - a new inverted-mapping post-pass is required to detect and exclude these as 'destination_collisions', separate from the existing 'ambiguous' stat

Acoustic fingerprinting design gap and resolution (Phase 1): a fingerprint computed only from scanned/new candidates has nothing to compare against because the OLD collection's original media is exactly what may be unreachable (that's why reconnection exists). Fingerprinting is therefore old-side-gated: only attempted when the old track's recorded path is still resolvable on disk at scan time; otherwise it is silently absent for that track (counted in stats, not an error) and matching falls through to the tag-based cascade

Fingerprint comparison semantics: duration must agree within +/-1.0s before comparing; similarity score >0.95 counts as a match; 0.80-0.95 is logged as fingerprint_near_match for human review only, never auto-accepted; a fingerprint result is only eligible to drive a rewrite when both sides have a computed fingerprint AND duration tolerance is satisfied AND similarity exceeds threshold - failing any one, the tier contributes nothing and matching falls through to the next cascade tier

VOLUME/VOLUMEID must both be explicitly set on every rewritten LOCATION; inference from an existing collection entry whose decoded path prefixes the scan root is allowed ONLY when unambiguous (exactly one distinct VOLUME/VOLUMEID pair observed under that prefix) - otherwise an explicit --volume-map flag is required, the tool must error rather than guess

Splice's identity/dedup reuses record_keys' tier ordering (the function, not match_records itself, since splice needs N-way grouping across multiple input files rather than pairwise old-vs-new comparison)

Splice conflict policy: fail-by-default; --on-conflict keep-first|keep-last is explicit opt-in; a persistent conflict report (key=value + CSV) is ALWAYS written regardless of policy, recording every conflicting identity group and which attributes differ, so a discarded side's data is never silently lost

Playlist-import algorithm for splice (fully specified, 6 steps): (1) every NODE TYPE=PLAYLIST anywhere in a non-base input's PLAYLISTS tree qualifies for import, no folder-location filtering; (2) non-colliding playlists are inserted as new children of the base's root FOLDER's SUBNODES, flattened one level (folder nesting not preserved per Phase 2 scope boundary); (3) PRIMARYKEY entries are retained verbatim unless their referenced track lost an identity conflict, in which case they're redirected to the winner's key via the existing old_to_new_key + cascade-redirect idiom; (4) same-name collisions get a deterministic '<name> (2)' rename with a freshly regenerated UUID (never reuse the source UUID - would create a duplicate within the output file); (5) any playlist reference that fails to resolve to a surviving COLLECTION entry after redirection aborts the entire write (zero-write-on-error) and is reported by playlist name + KEY; (6) SORTING_INFO entries are copied/rewritten to match a renamed/relocated playlist's new PATH, or explicitly dropped and reported - never silently orphaned

Textual-fidelity policy for splice/split (Phase 2): span transplantation (byte-exact copying of source XML spans, generalizing the existing _find_opening_tag_end-style scanning to find matching closing tags) is the DEFAULT for every unmodified fragment; ET.tostring() serialization is retained only as an explicit, lower-fidelity fallback used solely for fragments actually modified (a rename, a PRIMARYKEY redirect) - split is therefore fully byte-preserving for every kept fragment (nothing foreign, nothing renamed), while splice is byte-preserving except for the specific renamed/redirected bytes

Two distinct count attributes exist in the real schema and both must be recalculated on any structural change: SUBNODES COUNT=N (child-node count on a FOLDER) and PLAYLIST ENTRIES=N (track count on a playlist), in addition to the already-known COLLECTION ENTRIES=N

Dangling-reference policy for split: default 'exclude' (drop non-selected refs, always yields a valid file, never duplicates audio); 'pull-in' is opt-in and explicitly documented as reintroducing cross-output divergence risk; 'fail' is strict validation. A playlist reduced to zero kept entries is omitted from output entirely (not written empty) and reported as playlist_dropped=<name>; partial retention is reported as playlist_partial=<name>:<kept>/<total>, never silent

Phase 0 refactors (widen EntryRecord.entry to Optional; unify _process_non_collection_rule_entries/_process_non_collection_compare_entries; unify cmd_rewrite/cmd_rewrite_from_collection_compare into write_nml_safely) are opportunistic, not a hard blocker for Phase 1 - Phase 1 reuses the existing compare-based cascade and write path completely unchanged, so it does not require Phase 0 to land first, though doing Phase 0 first is still recommended since it's justified by pre-existing duplication independent of Phase 1

Tradeoff accepted: Phase 2's scope boundary is a flat playlist-entry merge/subset tool, NOT full playlist-tree preservation - nested folder structure beyond a playlist's own immediate node, smartlist/dynamic-playlist criteria, and SORTING_ORDER/track-index metadata beyond append-order are explicitly out of scope for v1; cue/beatgrid/loop analysis metadata living on ENTRY itself is carried through unmodified as part of copying the entry, never separately recomputed
